newsitem.title: UK: Bass may face rap over alcopop motif - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bass may face rap over alcopop motif - paper.

text.p: British brewing group Bass Plc may be publicly admonished this week by an industry body for its packaging of "Hoopers Hooch" -- alcoholic fruit-flavoured drinks or "alcopops," the Financial Times newspaper said.
The Portman Group, a body funded by seven leading brewers and distillers to promote sensible drinking, will publish first rulings on complaints over packaging on Wednesday.
A spokeswoman for the group declined to comment on the newspaper report.

Bass, which is a founder member of the Portman Group, said it was "confident that all of our alcoholic drinks meet or exceed the terms" of a code on packaging and marketing of alcoholic drinks published earlier this year.
A spokeswoman for Bass said it would "respond accordingly" once the rulings were known.
The Financial Times said the company was likely to drop the Hoopers Hooch motif -- a smiling face on a fruit -- rather than negotiate an acceptable form.
Hooper's Hooch holds 70 percent of the fast-growing alcopops market -- said to be worth around 250 million stg a year.
It comes in orange, lemon and blackcurrant flavour.
Alcopops have been sharply criticised by alcohol concern groups who say they target under-age drinkers. Alcohol in Britain can be sold only to those over the age of 18.
